t: Bornu kingdom ends as independent state
c: It was known as the Kanem Empire from the 9th century AD onward and lasted as the independent kingdom of Bornu until 1893.

t: Royal Chronicle discovered by Heinrich Barth
c: The history of the Empire is mainly known from the Royal Chronicle or Girgam discovered in 1851 by the German traveller Heinrich Barth.

t: Kanem peaks under Dunama Dibalemi
c: Kanem reached its peak under Mai (king) Dunama Dibalemi ibn Salma.

t: Kongolo Mwamba unifies Luba peoples
c: Sometime between 1300 and 1400 AD, Kongolo Mwamba (Nkongolo) from the Balopwe clan unified the various Luba peoples, near Lake Kisale.

t: Mwene Muji emerges near Lake Mai-Ndombe
c: To its east around Lake Mai-Ndombe, there emerged Mwene Muji, likely around 1400.

t: Afonso I, a Christian, takes Kongo throne
c: In 1506, Afonso I, a Christian, took over the throne.

t: Jaga invade and devastate Kongo
c: About 1568 to 1569, the Jaga invaded Kongo, laying waste to the kingdom and forcing the manikongo into exile.

t: Portuguese mercenaries reinstate Manikongo Álvaro I
c: In 1574, Manikongo Álvaro I was reinstated with the help of Portuguese mercenaries.

t: Solomonic dynasty begins rule in Ethiopia
c: From 1270 AD and on for many centuries, the Solomonic dynasty ruled the Ethiopian Empire.

t: Emperor Yeshaq I sends emissaries to Aragon
c: In 1428, the Emperor Yeshaq I sent two emissaries to Alfonso V of Aragon, who sent return emissaries who failed to complete the return trip.

t: Ethiopia begins continuous relations with Portugal
c: The first continuous relations with a European country began in 1508 with the Kingdom of Portugal under Emperor Lebna Dengel, who had just inherited the throne…

t: Emperor Susenyos converts to Roman Catholicism
c: When Emperor Susenyos converted to Roman Catholicism in 1624, years of revolt and civil unrest followed resulting in thousands of deaths.

t: Umayyad Caliphate conquers North Africa
c: By 711 AD, the Umayyad Caliphate had conquered all of North Africa.

t: Death of Abu Bakr causes political breakdown
c: The death of Abu Bakr in 1087 saw a breakdown of unity and increase military dissension in the south.

t: Portugal captures Ceuta from North Africa
c: Around 1415, Portugal engaged in a reconquista of North Africa by capturing Ceuta, and in later centuries Spain and Portugal acquired other ports on the North…

t: Spain defeats Granada, ends Muslim rule Iberia
c: In 1492, at the end of the Granada War, Spain defeated Muslims in the Emirate of Granada, effectively ending eight centuries of Muslim domination in southern…

t: Moulay al-Rashid reunites Morocco, founds Alaouite
c: Later it was reunited by Moulay al-Rashid, founder of the Alaouite dynasty.

t: Ismail ibn Sharif strengthens Moroccan unity
c: His brother and successor, Ismail ibn Sharif, strengthened the unity of the country by importing slaves from the Sudan to build up the military.

t: Rashidun Caliphate conquers Byzantine Egypt
c: In 642 AD, the Rashidun Caliphate conquered Byzantine Egypt.

t: Saladin defeats crusaders and recaptures Jerusalem
c: Saladin defeated the Christian crusaders at Egypt's borders and recaptured Jerusalem in 1187.

t: Saladin establishes Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt
c: On the death of Al-Adid, the last Fatimid caliph, in 1171, Saladin became the ruler of Egypt, ushering in the Ayyubid dynasty.

t: Mamluks overthrow Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt

t: Egypt halts Mongols at Battle of Ain Jalut
c: Egypt extended her territories to Syria and Palestine, thwarted the crusaders, and halted a Mongol invasion in 1260 at the Battle of Ain Jalut.

t: Egypt becomes part of Ottoman Empire
c: In 1517, at the end of an Ottoman–Mamluk War, Egypt became part of the Ottoman Empire.

t: British and Ottoman empires remove French occupation
c: However, the British Empire and the Ottoman Empire were able to remove French occupation in 1801.

t: Kingdom establishes capital at Sennar
c: Between 1504 and 1505, the kingdom expanded, reaching its peak and establishing its capital at Sennar under Badi II Abu Daqn.

t: Army reduces Badi IV to figurehead
c: Under Badi IV, the army turned on the king, making him nothing but a figurehead.

t: Muhammad Ali conquers Funj sultanate
c: In 1821, the Funj were conquered by Muhammad Ali, Pasha of Egypt.

t: Early ironworks in KwaZulu-Natal emerge
c: They slowly moved south, and the earliest ironworks in modern-day KwaZulu-Natal Province are believed to date from around 1050.

t: Leopard's Kopje people settle Bambandyanalo
c: Around 1000, some Leopard's Kopje people moved south to settle Bambandyanalo (known as K2), as the Zhizo moved west to settle Toutswe in modern-day Botswana.

t: Great Zimbabwe founded
c: Great Zimbabwe was founded around 1000 AD, and construction on the city's iconic dry-stone walls began in the 11th century.

t: Mapungubwe royal elites relocate to hill
c: Amid a harsh drought which likely troubled the society, royal elites moved the capital to Mapungubwe Hill and settled its flat-topped summit around 1220, while…

t: Mapungubwe produces textiles and ceramics
c: By 1250, Mapungubwe had a population of 5000, and produced textiles and ceramics.

t: Trade routes shift north, Great Zimbabwe rises
c: By 1300, trade routes had shifted north as merchants bypassed the Limpopo and Mapungubwe by travelling the Save River into the gold-producing interior,…

t: Sotho-Tswana states develop on highveld
c: The development of Sotho–Tswana states based on the highveld, south of the Limpopo River, began around 1000 CE.

t: Dutch establish permanent settlement at Table Bay
c: In order to control the price of meat and stock and make service more consistent, the Dutch established a permanent settlement at Table Bay in 1652.

t: Portugal attacks Kilwa on Swahili coast
c: On a mission to economically control and Christianize the Swahili coast, the Portuguese attacked Kilwa first in 1505 and other cities later.

t: Omani Arabs remove Portuguese presence
c: With the help of Omani Arabs, by 1729 the Portuguese presence had been removed.

t: Mary Leakey publishes archaeological findings at Urewe, Kenya
c: Urewe is the name of the site in Kenya brought to prominence through the publication in 1948 of Mary Leakey's archaeological findings.

t: Arab and Indian settlements in Madagascar
c: About the year 1000, Arab and Indian trade settlement were started in northern Madagascar to exploit the Indian Ocean trade.

t: All Madagascar regions inhabited
c: By 1100, all regions of Madagascar were inhabited, although the total population remained small.

t: Portuguese raid island trading settlements
c: In 1500, the Portuguese were the first Europeans on the island, raiding the trading settlements.

t: Radama I invites Christian missionaries
c: Radama I invited Christian missionaries in the early 19th century.

t: Queen Ranavalona I bans Christianity in Madagascar
c: Queen Ranavalona I "the Cruel" banned the practice of Christianity in the kingdom, and an estimated 150,000 Christians perished.

t: Madagascar takes French orientation under Radama II
c: Under Radama II, Madagascar took a French orientation, with great commercial concession given to the French.

t: France invades Madagascar and declares protectorate
c: In 1895, in the second Franco-Hova War, the French invaded Madagascar, taking over Antsiranana (Diego Suarez) and declaring Madagascar a protectorate.

t: States arise on Great Lakes plateau
c: By 1000 AD, numerous states had arisen on the Lake Plateau among the Great Lakes of East Africa.

t: Mwami Ruganzu II founds Kingdom of Rwanda
Mwami Mutara II completes Rwandan unification
c: The last Tutsi chief gave up to Mwami Mutara II (Mutara Rwogera) in 1852, but the last Hutu holdout was conquered in the 1920s by Mwami Yuhi V (Yuli Musinga).

t: Tutsi chief Ntare Rushatsi founds kingdom
Portuguese welcomed back for trade
c: In 1640, he welcomed back the Portuguese for trade.

t: War Jabi of Takrur adopts Sunni Islam
c: In 1035 king War Jabi of Takrur became the first ruler to adopt Sunni Islam.

t: Conflict erupts in Mali's Keita dynasty
c: In Mali after the death of Musa II in 1387, vicious conflict ensued within the Keita dynasty.

t: Islam becomes court religion under Uli I
c: Islam became a court religion under Sundiata's son Uli I.

t: Mansa Musa comes to power in Mali
c: In 1312 Mansa Musa came to power in Mali after his predecessor had set out on an Atlantic voyage.

t: Songhai Empire captures Niani
c: In 1545 to 1546, the Songhai Empire took Niani.

t: Sonni Ali captures Timbuktu from Tuareg
c: Sonni Ali, a Songhai, began his conquest by capturing Timbuktu in 1468 from the Tuareg.

t: Askia Mohammad I deposes Sonni Ali's heirs
c: After his death in 1492, his heirs were deposed by his nephew a General Askia Mohammad I, son of kassey, a Sonni Ali sister.

t: Muhammad Ture founds Askiya dynasty Songhai
c: Muhammad Ture founded the Askiya dynasty, askiya being the title of the king.

t: Askiya Muhammad is deposed by his son
c: Askiya Muhammad was deposed by his son in 1528.

t: Askiya Daoud assumes Songhai throne
c: After much rivalry, Muhammad Ture's last son Askiya Daoud assumed the throne.

t: Morocco invades Songhai under Ahmad al-Mansur
c: In 1591, Morocco invaded the Songhai Empire under Ahmad al-Mansur of the Saadi dynasty in order to secure the goldfields of the Sahel.

t: Usman dan Fodio accuses Hausa leadership
c: In the city of Gobir, Usman dan Fodio accused the Hausa leadership of practicing an impure version of Islam and of being morally corrupt.

t: Usman dan Fodio launches Fulani War
c: In 1804, he launched the Fulani War as a jihad among a population that was restless about high taxes and discontented with its leaders.

t: Britain conquers Sokoto Caliphate
c: The Sokoto Caliphate lasted until 1903 when the British conquered northern Nigeria.

t: Osei Kofi Tutu I unifies Ashante Confederation
Ashante conquer Denkyira, gain coastal trade
c: In 1701, the Ashante conquered Denkyira, giving them access to the coastal trade with Europeans, especially the Dutch.

t: Opoku Ware I expands Ashante Empire
c: Opoku Ware I engaged in further expansion, adding other southern Akan states to the growing empire.

t: Asantehene Opoku attacks Dagomba
c: Between 1744 and 1745, Asantehene Opoku attacked the powerful northern state of Dagomba, gaining control of the important middle Niger trade routes.

t: Osei Kwadwo imposes administrative reforms
c: Osei Kwadwo imposed administrative reforms that allowed the empire to be governed effectively and to continue its military expansion.

t: Ashante rulers continue territorial consolidation
c: Osei Kwame Panyin, Osei Tutu Kwame, and Osei Bonsu continued territorial consolidation and expansion.

t: King Houegbadja organizes Dahomey as centralized state
King Agadja attempts to end slave trade
c: King Agadja attempted to end the slave trade by keeping the slaves on plantations producing palm oil, but the European profits on slaves and Dahomey's…

t: Oyo Empire conquers Dahomey
c: In 1730, under king Agaja, Dahomey was conquered by the Oyo Empire, and Dahomey had to pay tribute.

t: France conquers Dahomey
c: France conquered Dahomey during the Second Franco-Dahomean War and established a colonial government there.

t: Ile-Ife founded as first Yoruba state
c: The first Yoruba state was Ile-Ife, said to have been founded around 1000 AD by a supernatural figure, the first oni Oduduwa.

t: Nupe kingdom conquers Oyo state
c: The Oyo state had been conquered in 1550 by the kingdom of Nupe, which was in possession of cavalry, an important tactical advantage.

t: Alafin Orompoto builds cavalry-based army
British protectorate established in Botswana
c: It became a protectorate of Great Britain in 1888, before further fragmenting into warring factions.

t: Oba Ewuare organizes Benin for conquest
Oba Esigie reduces council power, opens trade
c: Ewuare's grandson Oba Esigie eroded the power of the uzama (state council) and increased contact and trade with Europeans, especially with the Portuguese who…

t: Germany declares German South West Africa protectorate
c: By 1884, the Germans declared the coastal region from the Orange River to the Kunene River a German protectorate, part of German South West Africa.

t: Rinderpest impacts Herero and Nama economies
c: Between 1896 and 1897, rinderpest impaired the Herero and Nama economy and slowed white expansion.

t: Shaka assassinated by half-brother Dingane
c: In 1828, Shaka was assassinated by his half brother Dingane, who lacked the military genius and leadership skills of Shaka.

t: Dingane killed in Zulu civil war
c: Dingane was killed in 1840 during a civil war.

t: Britain invades Zulu Kingdom
c: In 1879 the Zulu Kingdom was invaded by Britain in a quest to control all of South Africa.

t: Moshoeshoe I founds Sotho Kingdom
c: One of the major states to emerge from the Mfecane was the Sotho Kingdom founded at Thaba Bosiu by Moshoeshoe I around 1821 to 1822.

t: Moshoeshoe requests British annexation of Sotho Kingdom
c: In 1868, Moshoeshoe asked that the Sotho Kingdom be annexed by Britain, to save the remnant.

t: First written records of modern-day Botswana appear
c: The first written records relating to modern-day Botswana appear in 1824.

t: Tswana chiefdoms resist Afrikaner incursions
c: In 1852 a coalition of Tswana chiefdoms led by Sechele I resisted Afrikaner incursions, and after about eight years of intermittent tensions and hostilities,…

t: Kololo conquer Barotseland
c: In 1845, the Kololo conquered Barotseland.

t: Moshoeshoe establishes capital at Butha-Buthe
c: In 1822, Moshoeshoe established his capital at Butha-Buthe, an easily defensible mountain in the northern Drakensberg mountains, laying the foundations of the…

t: Missionaries develop Sesotho orthography and materials

t: Lesotho becomes British protectorate

t: British take Cape Colony from Dutch
c: In 1795, the British took over the cape colony from the Dutch.

t: Britain defeats Boer republics in Second Boer War
c: In 1901, the Boer republics were defeated by Britain in the Second Boer War.

t: Ruanda-Urundi established as Belgian mandate

c:
